definitions.explanation: An official warning issued by authorities, especially the Japan Meteorological Agency, to alert the public about potential weather hazards. Less severe than a {警報|けいほう} (warning).

examples.japanese: {大雨|おおあめ}{注意報|ちゅういほう}が{出|で}た。
examples.english: A heavy rain advisory was issued.

examples.japanese: {強風|きょうふう}{注意報|ちゅういほう}が{発令|はつれい}されている。
examples.english: A strong wind advisory has been issued.

examples.japanese: {今朝|けさ}から{波浪|はろう}{注意報|ちゅういほう}が{出|で}ているので、{海|うみ}には{近|ちか}づかないでください。
examples.english: A wave advisory has been in effect since this morning, so please stay away from the ocean.

notes:
USAGE:
In Japan's weather alert system, {注意報|ちゅういほう} is a lower-level alert than {警報|けいほう} (warning), which in turn is lower than {特別警報|とくべつけいほう} (special warning). Common types include {大雨|おおあめ}{注意報|ちゅういほう} (heavy rain advisory), {強風|きょうふう}{注意報|ちゅういほう} (strong wind advisory), and {雷|かみなり}{注意報|ちゅういほう} (thunder advisory).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {注意報|ちゅういほう}が{出|で}る (an advisory is issued)
- {注意報|ちゅういほう}が{解除|かいじょ}される (an advisory is lifted)
- {注意報|ちゅういほう}を{発令|はつれい}する (to issue an advisory)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {警報|けいほう}: warning — a more severe level of alert, indicating greater danger
- {特別警報|とくべつけいほう}: special warning — the highest level, for extraordinary danger
